item.text: The controls each currently own their async handler, and the confirmation promise is awaited before `startUpdating`; that leaves the exact rapid-click window described. I’m checking the remaining Mute implementation and how the parent panel tracks the selected member so the lock can cover all three controls for that member.

The shared lock is now owned by the admin tools container, keyed to the member, and acquired synchronously before confirmation so same-tick clicks cannot race React rendering. I’m tightening settlement handling next: the controls must stay locked until the underlying request settles, and cancel/error paths need to release exactly once.

item.text: The target panel now disables all three controls together and keeps independent pending locks for separate members. Confirmation cancellation returns through `finally` without sending a request; request failures are caught by the existing handlers, show one error dialog, and release the lock. Existing panel tests and type checks are running.
Both checks are taking longer than usual and have not reported failures yet. While they finish, I’m doing a final diff review for promise settlement and formatting issues.
